# `node/no-unpublished-bin`

**A package's `bin` file is one npm publishes**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-node` (npm) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | no preset — name it in `[rules]` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (whether to publish the file or point `bin` elsewhere is the package author's decision) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-n/no-unpublished-bin` |

## What it checks

A file that the nearest `package.json` names in `bin` (directly, without `.js`, or as a folder's `index.js`) but that its `files` list leaves out of the published package is reported at its start: the installed command would point at nothing. `.npmignore` is not read; a package without `files` publishes everything, so it is left alone.

**Why:** npm creates the command's link to a file it did not ship, and the command fails after install.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-node
```

**No preset turns it on.** Load its pack through any preset (`codelaw:node/recommended` here), then name the rule in `[rules]`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:node/recommended"]

[rules]
"node/no-unpublished-bin" = "error"
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"node/no-unpublished-bin" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "node/no-unpublished-bin" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"node/no-unpublished-bin" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"node/no-unpublished-bin" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"node/no-unpublished-bin" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "node/no-unpublished-bin": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore node/no-unpublished-bin: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore node/no-unpublished-bin expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule node/no-unpublished-bin --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain node/no-unpublished-bin       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule node/no-unpublished-bin  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>           # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Add the file (or its folder) to `files` in package.json, or point `bin` at a published file.

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

```js files
// package.json
{ "name": "tool", "bin": "cli.js", "files": ["lib"] }
// cli.js
run();
```

#### Do

```js files
// package.json
{ "name": "tool", "bin": "cli.js", "files": ["lib", "cli.js"] }
// cli.js
run();
```

### JSX

#### Don't

```jsx files
// package.json
{ "name": "tool", "bin": "cli.jsx", "files": ["lib"] }
// cli.jsx
run();
```

#### Do

```jsx files
// package.json
{ "name": "tool", "bin": "cli.jsx", "files": ["lib", "cli.jsx"] }
// cli.jsx
run();
```

### TypeScript

#### Don't

```ts files
// package.json
{ "name": "tool", "bin": "cli.ts", "files": ["lib"] }
// cli.ts
run();
```

#### Do

```ts files
// package.json
{ "name": "tool", "bin": "cli.ts", "files": ["lib", "cli.ts"] }
// cli.ts
run();
```

### TSX

#### Don't

```tsx files
// package.json
{ "name": "tool", "bin": "cli.tsx", "files": ["lib"] }
// cli.tsx
run();
```

#### Do

```tsx files
// package.json
{ "name": "tool", "bin": "cli.tsx", "files": ["lib", "cli.tsx"] }
// cli.tsx
run();
```
